recentItems.title: LARGE WAREHOUSES DESTROYED! New routes and supply restoration for Ukrainian businesses
recentItems.description:
The destruction of large warehouses is already changing the supply system in Ukraine. In a special report — the consequences of strikes on distribution centers of supermarkets, food enterprises, grain storage facilities, logistics complexes, and humanitarian aid sites. After losing major hubs, companies are forced to transport products from other regions, distribute stock among smaller warehouses, and map out alternative routes. This makes delivery longer and more expensive, and may lead to the temporary disappearance of certain items from store shelves. At the same time, the report emphasizes that this is not about a food shortage in Ukraine, but primarily about pressure on its storage and delivery system. The report shows how retail chains and manufacturers adapt after strikes, restore supply chains, and shift from large centralized warehouses to more decentralized logistics.

recentItems.title: MOSCOW OIL REFINERY HIT—Vivaldi reclaims territory, while Russian troops in the south lose logistics
recentItems.description:
The Ukrainian Defense Forces reported a strike on the Moscow Oil Refinery in Kapotnya, where a large-scale fire broke out following the attack, damaging oil processing units. Reuters confirms damage to part of the Moscow Oil Refinery during a large-scale attack on September 20. The report also highlights the deployment of Ukrainian long-range systems, including "Flamingo" and the new "Pelican"/FP-7. On the front line, Operation "Vivaldi" continues: the command of the 3rd Army Corps reports 125 km² of territory returned to Ukrainian control. Additionally, the coverage details Operation "Blackbird" targeting the energy supply of Russian troops in the south, as well as a sabotage operation at the railway hub in Taganrog. Meanwhile, Russia continues its massive strikes against Ukraine: in this episode — a tragedy in the Kyiv region, a repeat strike on rescuers in the Zaporizhzhia region, and an FPV drone attack on a monastery in the Kherson region.

recentItems.title: Occupied Kherson region: thousands of people waiting for evacuation | LIVE
UKRAINE REVEALS OPERATION "VIVALDI" — 85 km², STRIKE ON SIX AIRCRAFT!
recentItems.description:
Ukraine has for the first time disclosed details of Operation "Vivaldi," which took place north of Lyman over several months under strict operational silence. Commander of the 3rd Army Corps, Andriy Biletsky, reported 75 km² of territory cleared of Russian infiltration groups and another 10 km² of liberated territory. Serednie was liberated, while Novoselivka, Oleksandrivka, Yarova, and the outskirts of Korovii Yar were cleared. ISW assesses that these actions disrupted Russian attempts to conduct a wide envelopment of the Ukrainian "fortress belt" in the Donetsk region.

Concurrently, Ukraine continues its strikes against Russian military infrastructure in the rear. The report covers an attack on a military airfield in Rostov-on-Don, following which the Ukrainian side claimed damage to an An-12, two An-26s, and three helicopters, as well as strikes on UAV control posts, ammunition depots, fuel infrastructure, and the Yaroslavl oil refinery. Additionally, we analyze the situation regarding Russian oil refining, fuel sales restrictions across a number of Russian regions, the state of the Black Sea Fleet, and how Ukraine and Europe are transitioning from delivering off-the-shelf weaponry to joint production of drones and air and missile defense systems.

recentItems.title: WASHINGTON INCREASES PRESSURE: new SANCTIONS on Russia AND BILLIONS for Ukraine’s air defense
recentItems.description:
US President Donald Trump has signed a comprehensive sanctions bill against Russia and Iran, named in honor of the late Senator Lindsey Graham. The document expands Washington's authority for economic pressure on Russia: sanction mechanisms target Russian officials, banks, and financial institutions, the energy and defense sectors, as well as "shadow fleet" vessels. A separate mechanism allows the US President to impose tariffs of up to 100% on the largest buyers of Russian oil and gas. The practical scope of these measures will depend on future decisions by the US administration.

Concurrently, the US has approved a potential sale of $2.68 billion in new equipment and weaponry to Ukraine to reinforce its air defense, while Denmark accelerates the delivery of a new aid package. Meanwhile, Poland joins the anti-ballistic coalition working on a unified European defense against ballistic missiles. Also in this episode: a massive Russian attack on Ukraine involving 174 drones and two "Zircon" missiles, the shortage of Patriot missiles, unidentified drones that temporarily suspended flights at Luxembourg Airport, and the first F-35A delivered to Germany.

recentItems.title: Cheap drone vs $10 million system! Ukraine changes the MATHEMATICS OF WAR
recentItems.description:
The war is increasingly resembling a battle of price tags: Ukrainian fighters reported destroying a Russian "Osa" air defense system valued at around $10 million. What's most notable is that Ukraine's defenders accomplished this using a drone costing just a few hundred dollars.

In another sector, Ukrainian operators targeted self-propelled artillery, trucks, communication systems, and Russian positions using FPV drones. Ukrainian forces also shot down a new Russian "Koshchey" reconnaissance drone, estimated to cost up to $40,000.

Meanwhile, Russian troops are preparing to shift their offensive from the spring-summer campaign straight into autumn and winter. We break down how mass-produced cheap drones are changing the cost-to-effect ratio on the modern battlefield and what to expect on the front lines in the near future.

recentItems.title: HUNDREDS OF DRONES heading toward MOSCOW as Ukraine secures €3.3B for missiles and drones
recentItems.description:
In this new episode of News Digest — one of the largest recent drone waves targeting Moscow. According to Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin, over 350 drones headed toward the Moscow region overnight, with the Russian side claiming 64 were intercepted on the city's approaches. That same night, strikes were reported against a military airfield in Rostov and Russian oil infrastructure.
New details have also emerged regarding the aftermath of the strike on the Yaroslavl "Slavneft-YANOS" refinery. The facility ceased crude oil refining following damage to key equipment, with the AVT-3 unit — which accounted for about 40% of the refinery's capacity — taken out of service.

At the same time, Ukraine is securing additional defense resources. The European Commission is allocating another €3.3 billion for the procurement of missiles and drones, while the EU plans to expand joint defense projects with Ukraine, particularly in anti-missile defense. This episode also covers reports of a potential new mobilization in Russia, Russian frontline casualties, the US military presence in Poland, and how new economic restrictions could impact Russia's oil export revenues.
